title: The Mystery of the Green Giants 🌳
text: Imagine you are standing outside. You look around and see tall, green giants everywhere. Some have colorful flowers, some give us sweet fruits, and some are so small you can hold them in your hand. But they never walk, talk, or run. How do they stay alive? Why are they everywhere?

title: What Do You Think?
text: If a plant can't walk to the kitchen like you do, how does it get its food? What would happen if there were no plants on Earth?

content.title: The Magic Plant Kitchen
content.description: Think of a plant like a house with its own magical kitchen. The roots are like straws drinking water from the ground, the stem is an elevator carrying the water up, and the leaves are the chefs cooking food using sunlight!

title: Meet the Plant Family
text: Plants come in different shapes and sizes! Trees are big and strong with thick trunks. Shrubs are bushy and medium-sized. Herbs are small with soft green stems. Climbers need support to grow up, while creepers grow along the ground.

content.definition: A tall plant with a thick, hard stem called a trunk (e.g., Mango tree, Neem tree). In Hindi, it's called 'Ped' (Tree).
A medium-sized bushy plant with a hard, woody stem (e.g., Rose, Tulsi). In Hindi, it's called 'Jhaadi' (Shrub).

question: Which of these has a thick, hard stem called a trunk?
Which part of the plant is like a straw drinking water from the ground?

content.title: Think and Tell!
content.description: Explain in your own words how a tree is different from a small herb like mint or coriander. If you had to explain it to your younger sibling, what would you say?

title: The Web of Life
text: Did you know? In ancient Indian texts like the Vedas, plants are called our silent friends. They give us oxygen to breathe, wood for furniture, and medicines to heal us! The food you ate today came from a plant. We are all connected in this beautiful web of life.

content.title: The Nature Detective
content.description: Mini Challenge: Go outside or look out your window. Find one tree, one small herb, and one colorful flower. Draw them in your notebook and label the parts you see (Root, Stem, Leaf, Flower).

content.title: Teacher's Tip
content.text: The Banyan tree, India's national tree, can live for hundreds of years and its roots grow down from its branches!

content.title: Common Mistake
content.text: Many students think mushrooms are plants, but they are not! They belong to a different family called fungi because they don't make their own food using sunlight.
